To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the informational complexity of networked dynamical systems is governed by the leading eigenmode of the system's covariance matrix, and that this eigenmode is maximized near criticality.
the informational complexity of a dynamical networked system increases near criticality.

1) the informational complexity of a networked dynamical system can be computed as a function of the network's weights; 2) the informational complexity increases near criticality; 3) the informational complexity is governed primarily by the eigenmode of the covariance matrix corresponding to the leading eigenvector of the adjacency matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the informational complexity of complex systems and how the dynamics of such systems can be used to characterize their complexity.
the informational complexity of complex dynamical network systems, and how this is related to their critical dynamics.
the problem of how complex dynamical network systems can be characterized and understood by their informational complexity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the integrated information is a monotonically increasing function of the network size and that the information generated by the whole system is greater than that generated by its parts, and this is true for any network topology.

the information integration capacity of dynamical network is a function of the eigenmodes of the network covariance and adjacency matrix, and that the eigenmode corresponding the the largest eigenvalue of the network covariance matrix dominates the information integration capacity.
the information integration capacity of dynamical systems is governed by the dynamics of their network structure and is optimized near criticality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the informational complexity of complex dynamical systems can be quantitatively characterized by a spectral decomposition of its network dynamics, and this decomposition can be used to understand the role of network topological features and dynamics on the informational complexity of the whole system.
integrated information is a function of the network's adjacency and covariance matrices.
the informational complexity of a system can be quantified by the eigenmodes of the system's covariance matrix and the system's network topology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not the topology of a network per se that is important for the emergence of high informational complexity, but rather the dynamical regime in which the system operates.
integrated information, a measure of informational complexity, can be computed analytically as a function of system dynamics and network topology.
the informational complexity of a network is determined by a single eigenmode that governs the dynamics near criticality.
